sections.name: redisProvider, RedisModule
sections.title: Building the Redis connection
sections.what: Creates the connection from either a full Redis URL or separate settings, with retries that wait longer each time up to 3 seconds, and makes it available to the app.
sections.why: Likely reason: supports both a single URL style and separate host settings used in different environments.
sections.watch_out: Each request gives up after a few retries, so a Redis outage shows up quickly as errors.

summary: Creates the one shared Redis connection that the API uses for caching and queues.
purpose: Connects the app to Redis so features can store short-lived data.
why: The header describes it as cache and queue infrastructure, which is the stated purpose.
how: 1) Build a connection from REDIS_URL if set. 2) Otherwise use the host, port, password, and database settings. 3) Retry failed connections with a growing wait, capped at 3 seconds. 4) Share the connection and the Redis helper service across the app.
inputs: REDIS_URL, or REDIS_HOST, REDIS_PORT, REDIS_PASSWORD, and REDIS_DB.
outputs: A Redis connection and the RedisService helper.
risks: Each command gives up after 3 retries, so features fail when Redis is down. The connection setup is duplicated in the common module. Retry settings are not covered by any test shown.
debug: If cache calls fail, check that Redis is running and reachable with the configured settings. If connections keep retrying, check the host, port, and password.
